chunks.rationale: The rollup is the contract the view trusts. summarizeUsage now takes a UsageReport (and still unwraps a bare UsageByDay). Every total carries cachedInputTokens / cacheWriteTokens / wastedUsd. processedTokens is input+cacheRead+cacheWrite+output; the Tokens toggle must use that, not uncached+output. isUnreported is turns>0 and every cost/token field is 0 — put on the row so the view cannot re-derive it wrong. cacheMultiplier is (inputTokens + cachedInputTokens) / inputTokens, only when cachedInputTokens>0 and inputTokens>0: a token-volume ratio, not a dollar saving. days[].byProvider is the per-day series for the overlay chart. models/byDay come from byDay; projects/threads come from threadsByDay using last-seen labels.
risks: Project/thread costShare uses the byDay range total as the denominator. If Worker A's two maps disagree, a project's share can exceed 100% or the column will not sum to 1. Internally consistent tables would need a per-grouping total instead.
A provider with cachedInputTokens>0 and inputTokens===0 (all-cache, no uncached remainder) gets cacheMultiplier=null. Honest, but a cache-only day is invisible as a multiplier.

unwrapReport treats any object lacking byDay/threadsByDay as a bare UsageByDay. A future field on UsageReport that is not those two keys is fine; a malformed payload whose top-level keys look like days is also accepted, which is the legacy path the existing tests rely on.

chunks.rationale: Keeps the whole UsageReport (the contract commit's byDay unwrap was a placeholder). Headline is the selected metric plus '* if billed at full API rate' — the dollar figure is a subscription counterfactual. Unreported provider rows render 'kimi · N turns · usage not reported' with no $0.00 and no share bar. Tokens metric uses processedTokens. Daily chart is one SVG area per reported provider, with hit columns that keep data-usage-bar. Stat strip is processed / cached / uncached / output; cache savings stays on the provider row as 'N× cache'. Breakdown toggle is Model/Day/Project/Thread. Wasted column shows formatCostUsd only when wastedUsd>0.
risks: Overlapped (not stacked) areas: a cheap high-token provider can hide a expensive low-token one when the Tokens toggle is on, and vice versa on Cost. Legend is the only decoder.
Unreported rows in the table print 'usage not reported' in the cost cell. A 90-day table with many kimi models will read as a wall of that phrase.
The wasted explanation 'on runs that ended failed/stopped' lives on the <th title>, so it is hover-only. The column header is just 'Wasted'.

allUnreported (every provider is zero-usage) replaces the headline number with 'usage not reported' so a kimi-only range does not show $0.00. Mixed ranges still headline the reported sum, which is correct.
jsdom does not lay out SVG, so no test proves the areas are visible or the legend colours match the paths.

chunks.rationale: Extends the existing module: caveat under the headline, stat strip, SVG chart + overlay hits, legend, unreported provider row, breakdown header. Reuses --blue/--green/--amber/--danger/--text-muted rather than a new palette. Chart replaces the old bar flex; data-usage-bar hit columns stay so the empty-state test still holds.
risks: providerRow is now 5 columns (name / bar / value / share / cache). A provider without a multiplier leaves the last track empty, so share% alignment can drift versus a cache-reporting neighbour.
Day and project tables keep an empty second column (the 'detail' slot used by model/thread). Harmless, slightly odd.

chunks.rationale: Browser-dev fixture for the new states: claude with large cache + wastedUsd, grok with tokens and no cache fields, all-zero kimi with 41 turns, threadsByDay across nebula and ledger and several threads. Without this the view is built blind.
risks: byDay and threadsByDay are hand-aligned, not generated from one source. Drift here will not be caught by tests (tests use their own fixtures).

chunks.rationale: Pins the issue's named cases: all-zero provider stays in providers with turns and unreported=true; processed ≠ billable when cache fields are set; old entries missing the new keys load as 0; cacheMultiplier is null for grok; day/project/thread groupings and share maths. Existing range/malformed tests still pass because unwrapReport accepts a bare UsageByDay.
risks: Share assertions use byDay totals as the whole. They will go red if someone 'fixes' project/thread share to be relative to the grouping's own sum.

chunks.rationale: Existing 7/30/cost/tokens/empty cases stay. New cases: unreported kimi row has 'usage not reported' and not '$0.00'; caveat marker; wasted $1.50 cell; breakdown toggle walks model → day → project → thread.
risks: The unreported test scopes 'not $0.00' to the kimi row. A regression that prints $0.00 in the wasted column of another row would not fail it — by design, because zero waste is not 'unreported'.
The share-bar absence check uses querySelector("[class*='shareTrack']"). CSS-module hashes keep 'shareTrack' in the class today; a rename of the local class silently weakens the test.
Subscription plan-quota next to the dollar figure is out of scope: no CLI reports it today, so it would be invented. Follow-up once any provider exposes remaining quota.
The 90-day preset will look sparse until the store has 90 days of the new shape. Expected, not a view bug.
Renderer suite beyond usage*.test was not the other worker's surface, but appWiring.test.tsx does mount UsageView — a wiring regression would show up there, not in usageView.test.tsx.
Project/thread attribution is only as good as Worker A's threadsByDay writer. This half cannot invent spend for a thread the store never recorded.
